text:
incident-bot: 🚨 alert: circuit-breaker triggered: eu-west-1 serving cluster degraded (5xx spike, kv-cache thrash). paging oncall: @alice
alice: seeing 5xx ~15% and request latency p95 up 2.3x. metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/shot/eu-west-1
ben: confirmed, tail logs show repeated kernel OOM events on pool-gpu-2, but nodes still alive. suspect memory leak in runtime after recent kernel bump.
charlie: any customer-facing impact? SLAs?
emily: support reports multiple enterprise customers in EU seeing failed generations and timeouts. Some complaints about unexpected partial responses.
dana: ok start live mitigation plan: 1) reduce non-essential traffic (batching & non-prod) 2) enable regional rate-limit shaping 3) begin graceful drain of eu-west-1 for model-family-redwood-v2 4) reroute to eu-west-2 / us-west-1 as fallback
alice: copying runbook: INCIDENT-TRAFFIC-DRain v3 -> https://runbooks.redwood/traffic-drain
alice: I'll initiate regional shaping. Ben, can you validate drain command syntax? I want to set eu-west-1 weight to 10% then 0 over 10m.
ben: use redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west-1 --policy gradual --to-weight 0 --duration 10m --model redwood-v2
ben: sample: 
```
# reduce eu-west to 10% then 0
redwoodctl routing update --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-v2 --policy gradual --steps "10%,0%" --step-interval 5m
```
alice: initiating now. infra-bot: please mute autoscaler alerts for eu-west during drain to avoid noisy paging.
infra-bot: action taken: alerts muted for eu-west-1 (policy: drain-mute). Reason: planned mitigation. by alice.
charlie: also recommend increasing rate limits for high-priority enterprise tokens during reroute so they don't get throttled by new region rate caps.
emily: I have a list of affected enterprise tokens — pushing to ops channel now.
dana: let's apply temporary quota bump for enterprise tier (x2) while reroute. command?
ben: api call below:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/admin/quotas/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"tier":"enterprise","multiplier":2,"expires_in":"2h"}'
```
alice: applied initial shaping: /route update returned 202 accepted. starting step 1 -> eu-west weight 10%.
charlie: monitoring logs: error-rate dropping at edge, but new region us-west-1 is absorbing traffic fine. p95 in us-west increased slightly but within SLO for now.
dana: enable conservative rate limit for default tokens to protect backend while queues settle: set 25 rps global for non-enterprise.
ben: applied rate-limit via config service:
```
service: rate-limiter
scope: global
default_rps: 25
exceptions: [enterprise]
```
deploy-bot: notice: config change committed acl:ops by ben (commit: 7a1f3c2)
alice: starting graceful drain to 0 now (second step).
alice: running redwoodctl drain --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-v2 --force-checks=false
ben: small hiccup: drain commands showing ongoing kv-cache hits causing slow completions — switching to forced prefix-eviction to speed up drain.
ben: command: 
```
redwoodctl cache evict --region eu-west-1 --model redwood-v2 --mode prefix --prefix-len 128
```
infra-bot: cache-evict job queued (job id: evict-20260301-43). ETA ~45s.
emily: customers on EU are being notified via status page about partial disruptions and failover. Posting curl to update status: 
```
curl -X POST https://status.redwood/incidents \
  -d '{"id":"INC-2026-231","summary":"Partial EU region failover - routing traffic to fallback regions"}'
```
charlie: support note: label impacted customers and attach request logs for postmortem. I'll take that.
alice: traffic now at 0% in eu-west for redwood-v2. monitoring: error-rate in global dropped by 60% overall. p95 stable.
dana: good. next: plan for rolling provider fallback for edge routes that still point to eu-west provider. Ben, can you bump provider preference to us-west primary for 48h.
ben: executing provider reroute: 
```
redwoodctl provider set-preference --provider-id=primary-eu --priority 10 --fallback us-west-provider --ttl 48h
```
ben: done. routing table updated. deploy-bot: published route diff (commit 7a1f3c2 -> 7a1f3d0)
charlie: noticed an odd oscillation in a subset of requests: client SDK retries were retrying stale region hints; we added a forced cache flush for client region hints.
alice: push a small client-config to edge to prefer new routing hints for 30m
```
redwoodctl edge config update --key client-region-hint-ttl --value 30m
```
infra-bot: edge hint TTL updated.
emily: support update sent to customers: "We've rerouted traffic and applied temporary rate limits. If you're seeing ongoing errors, please send logs to support@redwood.com" :thumbsup:
dana: status check: any node restarts still happening in eu-west? we drained, but are there lingering evictions causing pod churn?
ben: one straggler node had kernel OOMs earlier; we cordoned the node and scheduled maintenance. Node will be rebooted once traffic normalized.
charlie: customers with strict data-region requirements — we need to flag those for follow up. Emily, can you collate list and outreach?
emily: on it. I've tagged impacted accounts and created tickets with priority P1 for any data residency customers.
alice: handoff: I'm going offline in ~15m. Dana, can you take incident lead for the next shift? I'll leave notes in the runbook with steps executed and commit ids.
dana: taking lead. please post summary of actions and timeline.
alice: summary: 1812345678 - circuit-breaker triggered eu-west-1; actions: muted alerts, set eu-west traffic 10%->0% over 10m, evicted KV prefix, applied global default rate-limit 25rps, bumped enterprise quotas x2, rerouted provider preference to us-west, updated client-region-hint TTL, customers notified. key commits: 7a1f3c2, 7a1f3d0. handing to @dana. :white_check_mark:
dana: noted. I'll monitor and keep alerts unmuted on escalation thresholds. next steps: schedule node reboots, postmortem run with runtime team, and plan for hotfix for kernel bump if repro confirmed.
charlie: adding to postmortem board. tagging runtime team: @ben @alice
emily: I'll follow up with affected customers and share the support tickets list.
incident-bot: incident acknowledged: incident-1812345678 -> assigned to dana. status: mitigated (traffic drained). metrics: https://grafana.redwood/shot/1812345678
dana: closing note: mitigation successful for now. we'll keep provider preference in place for 48h and monitor. if error-rate drops below 0.5% sustained and p95 < 1.2x baseline, we'll start reintroducing eu-west with canary traffic next window.
ben: creating patch branch to revert kernel bump for test envs and run stress tests.
alice: thanks team. good triage and fast response. :heart:
charlie: leaving notes for postmortem: timeline, decisions, customer impact, follow-ups (kernel rollback, node health checks, enhanced kv-cache metrics).
emily: I'll draft customer-facing incident summary once we have final postmortem. expected ETA 24-48h.
dana: handing to operations on-call for reintroducing region when safe. end of thread.
__notes: No title field included per agents.md. Thread messages are a single continuous string with sender prefixes.
